lessons.title: Narrative past: strong verbs
lessons.objective: Narrative past: strong verbs: In the passato remoto, strong verbs use a memorized stem only in io, lui/lei and loro (ebbi, ebbe, ebbero) and the regular stem in tu, noi and voi (avesti, avemmo, aveste).
lessons.explanation:
In the passato remoto, strong verbs use a memorized stem only in io, lui/lei and loro (ebbi, ebbe, ebbero) and the regular stem in tu, noi and voi (avesti, avemmo, aveste). This narrative past tells stories, history and formal reports; regular verbs end in -ai, -asti, -ò (-are), -ei, -esti, -é (-ere), -ii, -isti, -ì (-ire).

This narrative past tells stories, history and formal reports; regular verbs end in -ai, -asti, -ò (-are), -ei, -esti, -é (-ere), -ii, -isti, -ì (-ire). Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. lessons.objective: Imperfect subjunctive: Take the imperfect stem (parla-, prende-, parti-) and add -ssi, -ssi, -sse, -ssimo, -ste, -ssero.

lessons.title: Conditional perfect
lessons.objective: Conditional perfect: Use avrei, avresti, avrebbe, avremmo, avreste, avrebbero or sarei, saresti, sarebbe, saremmo, sareste, sarebbero plus the participle for a hypothetical completed action.
lessons.explanation:
Use avrei, avresti, avrebbe, avremmo, avreste, avrebbero or sarei, saresti, sarebbe, saremmo, sareste, sarebbero plus the participle for a hypothetical completed action. Italian also uses it for the future seen from the past: Ha detto che sarebbe venuto.
parlare · io: avrei parlato — to speak · Conditional perfect
mangiare · io: avrei mangiato — to eat · Conditional perfect
lessons.speakingPrompt: Use Conditional perfect while discussing imagining a different schedule. You and an Italian-speaking classmate are discussing imagining a different schedule. Use avrei, avresti, avrebbe, avremmo, avreste, avrebbero or sarei, saresti, sarebbe, saremmo, sareste, sarebbero plus the participle for a hypothetical completed action. Italian also uses it for the future seen from the past: Ha detto che sarebbe venuto. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.explanation:
Verbs in -ciare, -giare and -iare drop the stem i when the ending already starts with i: cominci, cominciamo; mangi, mangiamo; cambi, cambiamo. The i stays in every other form, and verbs with a stressed i such as inviare keep both (invii).

lessons.explanation:
Verbs in -care and -gare add h before an ending that starts with i or e, to keep the hard sound: cerchi, cerchiamo; paghi, paghiamo. The h also appears in the whole future and conditional: cercherò, pagherei.

lessons.objective: Irregular past participles · independent practice: Many common verbs have an irregular participle that must be memorized: fatto, detto, messo, preso, visto, scritto, letto, chiuso, aperto, rotto.
lessons.explanation:
Many common verbs have an irregular participle that must be memorized: fatto, detto, messo, preso, visto, scritto, letto, chiuso, aperto, rotto. Use it with ho, hai, ha, abbiamo, avete, hanno like a regular participle.

lessons.speakingPrompt: Use Irregular past participles while discussing explain a change of routine. You and an Italian-speaking classmate are discussing explain a change of routine. lessons.title: Regular -ire present · independent practice
lessons.objective: Regular -ire present · independent practice: Remove -ire; add -o, -i, -e, -iamo, -ite, -ono.
lessons.explanation:
Remove -ire; add -o, -i, -e, -iamo, -ite, -ono. These verbs take no -isc-, and only the voi ending -ite differs from the -ere pattern.
partire · io: parto — to leave / depart · Regular -ire present
dormire · io: dormo — to sleep · Regular -ire present
lessons.speakingPrompt: Use Regular -ire present while discussing compare a real plan with a hypothesis. You and an Italian-speaking classmate are discussing compare a real plan with a hypothesis. Remove -ire; add -o, -i, -e, -iamo, -ite, -ono. These verbs take no -isc-, and only the voi ending -ite differs from the -ere pattern. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.
